notes.title: Version 1.3.3 now available
notes.notes:
AFC2020-21 v1.3.3 is now live for PC and Linux! This fixes a couple major bugs - there should now be sound on Windows, and a missing line of code meant tribunals were being recorded, but weren't triggering. The new major quality of life addition - the player who has the ball's now labeled, which makes a big improvement when watching a match! Also, over-aged players were further down-weighted in the national draft.

Hope you enjoy the update!

VERSION 1.3.3
+ Improved: Further nerfed overage (>21 years) players in the national draft
+ Improved: Added player label for the player in possession of the ball
- Fixed: Commissioner mode check-box was not persistent between save games
- Fixed: Minor player statistic issue fixed
- Fixed: Premiership years were disappearing on game load
- Fixed: Sound was not working on Windows
- Fixed: Tribunals weren't working, they were being created but the league that was supposed to review the tribunal wasn't saving

notes.title: 2021 update released!
notes.notes:
Ready for 2021?

The Australian Football Coach 2021 update features a full data update and a number of brand new features and fixes for PC and Linux!

Want to watch any game, not just your own team's? Now you can.

Want to compare team statistics? Check.

Want to see who won historical awards? It's all there.

Want to sub on a player? Done.

Not only that, but the player decision making code has been completely revamped, leading to a more realistic (and slightly, though possibly imperceptibly faster!) match engine. The AI list management has also improved, and sounds during the game make for a more realistic matchday experience!

Mac users should have the data update and will receive a full patch in a couple months due to issues with the port.

Hope you coach your way to many flags!

VERSION 1.3

+ Added: Crowd sounds (basic)
+ Added: Listed-retired status, adds a player to a team's list but makes them unable to play ("injures" them for the year with an injury of "retired") - does not exist naturally in the game, only added to allow players to have that status when loaded from a database to reflect 2021 list changes
+ Added: Team statistics now visible
+ Added: Contested marks statistic now visible in the game for players
+ Added: New awards screen
+ Added: 2021 substitution rule (should work, but not well-tested)
- Updated: All players now on new teams, some teams have updated contract extensions (working on it)
- Improved: Player decision-making code

- Improved: Improved match engine speeds through optimising several slow routines

- Improved: Fatigue has a larger impact on "active" players (disposing, tackling, etc)

notes.title: Version 1.2.5 released
notes.notes:
As the real life footy season winds to a close, development of Australian Football Coach 2020 also starts to wind down. The newest patch - the first in a month - now includes the 2018 season as formerly available seasons from the original version of the game continue to migrate over!

The patch also takes care of several reported issues. A couple of them were not positively confirmed before patching, so if you notice any issues, please get in touch.

As announced before, this update is only currently completely available to users on PC and Linux due to issues surrounding compiling the game for Mac. In addition, the 2018 season is not yet available on Mac, though the other data has been updated.

The full change log is below:
VERSION 1.2.5
- Fixed: U18 players now have separate delisting code so they can be signed by state teams
- Fixed: If you delisted a player who had most recently appeared in a state league game, the notification would display with the state league information
- Fixed: game would crash if player status in the file wasn't between or inclusive of the values 0 and 7
- Possibly fixed: Players would ask for the maximum contract immediately following the end of the season
- Possibly fixed: Players would get stuck in interchange mode when coaching a game
- Improved: Can now view team stats by year
- Improved: Per user request, adjusted size of height of awards panel on player screen
- Improved: If your team is performing very well, ambitious players will want to remain during the season
- Improved: Scenarios now sorted in alphabetical order on new game screen
+ Added: AI Trade Frequency setting (this works but the scale of this is untested - if you have it set to very rare and you're still getting a lot of trades drop a line)
+ Added: Updated historical team ladders database back to 2010 (to fix issue with 2014 season scenario)
+ Added: 2018 scenario (migrated from original AFC)

notes.title: New patch released & Early Access ends August 22!
notes.notes:
On August 22 Australian Football Coach will transition from Early Access to Full Release! If you haven't purchased yet you'll be able to pick the game up at a launch discount.

Version 0.11.0 is now live on the Steam servers as well! While this was intended to be a simple bug fix, this version went above and beyond a normal minor version so it had to be released as a major version. New features include a league overview screen, designed for when you want to sit back and watch the world simulate by; a pause simulation button, which literally lets you stop time; the ability to save lineups into one of three different slots; and an update to club shields, including a new shield which allows you to flip the primary and secondary text colours.

Bug fixes include issues with stadiums in custom leagues, team prestige never changing over time, and some issues with saving and loading, including with your team's list manager.

A hotfix is planned for later this week as well, as there's still a known crash when disbanding/adding teams to a league. Not entirely sure what the issue is yet, but as soon as it's patched version 0.11.1 will come out, along with some other possible bug fixes and minor feature additions.

There's still a small number of things to clean up before the game's full release, which will signify the end of the 2020 development cycle, though bug fixes will still be applied after the 22nd as needed. Thanks again for all your support!

notes.title: The list management update - v0.10.0 now released
notes.notes:
The AI list management update launched this weekend!

Many users have written in or discussed the game on [url=https://discord.gg/7GspWCK]Discord[/url], with the biggest complaint being that the AI didn't do a good enough job with offseason management. Superstars were being picked in the national draft, players weren't re-signing enough, state teams weren't being active in free agency, and trading was a bit of a mess.

That's all been fixed in the last patch! After over 50 distinct iterative simulations, the AI list managers have been made a lot smarter. New code was written to help the AI estimate just how good a player will be over time, which also impacts the length of their contract offer. Additionally, a bug was fixed where basically any player who was even barely homesick would not re-sign with an interstate team. As a result, a couple superstars will make it to free agency every year, but this will happen rarely as clubs try to lock down players who will help make their list better for years to come.

State clubs now do a better job of asking for free agents, including amateur leagues - there was a bug where they wouldn't re-sign any players at all.

The one area which still needs some work is AI trades with other AI clubs - the AI wants to make trades, but doesn't do a good job valuing draft picks and tends to avoid making draft pick trades entirely. Even then, the AI will now trade a lot less. Also, the AI will still draft mature aged players in the national draft, though this has also been significantly reduced - instead of picking the best available player, which could have been a delisted player who wasn't quite good enough to make a free agency signing, the list managers now consider potential much more strongly. The code for youth players has also been tweaked so the game doesn't keep recycling the same skill 70-75 players over and over again in the draft.

All in all, the game world has become a lot more realistic in just one patch. If you see any discrepancies or oddities, please get in touch on the Steam forums, on Facebook, or on Discord.

Those who love tracking history will also be happy to know you can now see the result of any draft for any league over time in this patch.

A tease for the future as well: There's probably one major patch between now and the game achieving v1.0 status. Once the game hits v1.0, the game will be complete and will not receive any further updates with the exception of bug fixes. The final features planned for AFC2020: league expansion/contraction, improved AI in-game tactical adjustments, reworked AI trades, and adding seasons 2015-2018 to the list of playable seasons, along with a planned 17-game 2020 season mod. If there's anything else you'd like to see added to the game this year, now's the time to get in touch!

Hope you enjoy the upgrade and as always a big thank you for all your support of the Australian Football Coach series.

notes.title: Patch v0.8.1 released
notes.notes:
Version 0.8.1 is out and the game's closer to moving out of early access! This patch makes renewing contracts more interesting as you'll get information on where the player stands with asking for a contract, and cleans up a lot of simulator issues. The game's scoring is down again after a fix regarding the hot spot and players have been taught to use the corridor less. They still use it slightly too much, but it's starting to get better.

Also fixed are issues with rucks getting too much of the ball because they were playing in multiple games due to a variable reset issue in new code and a contract bug where a player would accept any offer you made due to code not triggering properly.

Some issues are still known to exist, such as the "draft pick trades" bug - occasionally the game will decide the draft pick you're offering is incorrect and stops the trade from going through - and not being able to accept a job offer when unemployed (though this may have been fixed and didn't make it to the change log - need to double check.)

Change log here:

notes.title: New and improved match simulation and interchanges! - Version 0.7.0 Released
notes.notes:
Footy is back and so too is Australian Football Coach with several new and improved features!

One of the biggest requests, manual interchanges, has been added back into the game, making the game more interesting for hands-on coaches. Simply click on two players on the interchange tab to switch them out - it couldn't be simpler! The code is relatively fresh so there are a couple other improvements planned for the display, but this should make the game more interesting to a few users.

Another piece of feedback has been that the match engine isn't quite realistic enough, especially in terms of rucks getting too many disposals. A whole season's worth of games was simulated to see how exactly the match engine was working and then all of the disposals were normalised for pitch height/width to create a heat map. It turned out the rucks weren't quite hitting the ball far enough, so frequently won the first loose ball after winning the ruck. This has been fixed - rucks should still get a decent number of disposals as they're midfielders, but it should be much less extreme. Centre bounce player positioning has also been updated.

Benchmarking the game also allowed several other quirks with the match engine to be fixed, especially one which showed a particular bias - it turns out the ball wasn't bouncing randomly enough on the pitch, and that was impacting game results!

These tweaks have really helped make the simulation more realistic and those of you who are stat-minded should see a definite difference. There's still more work to be done, especially in regards to player positioning, and any feedback is welcome.

There's also a new match preview screen complete with predictions and information about your upcoming match, which means you don't jump straight into a game unless you're ready.

More good news as well, version 0.7.1 should be coming out in the next couple days as a couple things didn't get added in by the 0.7.0 release deadline, so be on the lookout for some new information/displays and headlines and (possibly) a complete overhaul and update of the 2020 lists!

Hope you enjoy the newest version!

notes.title: New version with Linux support! 0.6.0 released, 0.6.1 patch now live
notes.notes:
Australian Football Coach has its first new version upgrade since launch! After 15 patches of version 0.5, version 0.6 finally adds some new features, including Linux support!

To go along with supporting a new operating system, the game also adds support for a fantasy draft and a user-requested feature that, if selected, forces you to confirm your squad before each game. Some users prefer to simulate seasons and others prefer to play out each game live and this should make for a more enjoyable experience for the one-game-at-a-time players! Also, rivalry games now have an impact on coach perception - lose a big one to your hated rival and it might just be the last game of your coaching career (assuming your job was on the brink, of course.)

Several bugs have been fixed as well, especially in the match engine where some interchange issues were occurring, back pockets running to the bench but not interchanging, as well as the dreaded away team advantage. The game should also be more stable with a number of crashes patched.

The game's improving with each version so hope you enjoy your latest coaching career!

Changelogs:

notes.title: Patch 0.5.15 released - fixes two big match engine issues
notes.notes:
The newest patch has been released fixing the two most-reported match engine issues:
1. Players should no longer run off the field during kick-ins (haven't entirely confirmed this is fixed, but it doesn't happen anymore, and it should be fixed.)
2. Players were occasionally sitting on the bench the whole game.

This should conclude all of the major bug fixes from release meaning version 0.6 is next!

The next big features planned in the road map for v0.6:
- The "Coaches Meeting" tab was introduced but has a "coming soon" label - this is the most important feature that didn't make it into launch. You'll be able to coach players weekly on morale and training... or as always, simply leave it up to your assistants
- Start your game off with a fantasy draft
- More immersion with content and news articles

Also, the older AFC scenarios have started to transition to the new AFC2020 data format, starting with the 2014 season. While data updates won't be version-specific, some users enjoy season replays, and the data formats aren't wildly different, so you may see some older seasons appear in your new game list as time goes on. (You could, if you wanted to, create a season sim for any season in history if you tweaked the attributes properly.)

notes.title: Patch 0.5.9 (and 0.5.8, 0.5.7) released
notes.notes:
Three new patches have been released in the past few days which continue to fix and improve the game and get AFC2020 closer to a full release!

This doesn't fix everything, so please post if your game crashes at any point. A couple of the crashes fixed this time around would happen relatively frequently, so hoping things calm down.

The next big push will be to work on defensive positioning - too many goals are being scored because a player wins a 1-on-1 and then runs the ball into the goal untouched due to differences in acceleration/speed - and also to work on time on ground, as there appear to be a few issues there as the game currently focuses too much on fatigue/stamina and not enough on skill when determining who should rotate on.

Resolution is also an issue for many users, which is difficult to handle but will be a focus next week. If your screen size is 768 pixels high or you use a high resolution monitor, the game already supports a fix, but you have to hack the game's Settings.txt file to make it work. The work next week will make sure that it's easier for you to handle resolution issues.
